doc.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997

title: Mental preparation before a gig and tonight's band
summary: He says preparation is mental, he's a 'gamer', and he praises the Montalbano family he is playing with tonight.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Well we should wrap up, I know you have to go play some jazz.
Yeah. We just got started. This should be a ten hour interview.
Yeah this is great. Well we’ll do Part Two actually, you know when you come back. We think about, you’re on your way to the gig, and how much preparation in your mind are you doing? Is there any?

It’s mental. It’s all mental to me. Like five or ten minutes before the gig I start thinking about tunes. There’s a feel that you get when you walk into the club, there’s a feeling of first of all, the audience helps. I mean if there’s an audience there you feel, mmm, okay, I’ve got to play tonight. Not that you don’t have to play if there’s no audience, but you just feel an obligation — there’s people there spending money, okay, you’ve got to bring it up to this notch, you know, immediately. But I start thinking of tunes, and just different things to do to make this night a little bit more unique than last night. And I’ve always been a gamer in the sense that if I was a football player, I wouldn’t want to go to practice, I’d be late. But when it came time to play the game I’ll kill ya. I’m ready to play. So that’s the way I am musically. I don’t do any preparation as far as, you know, like I wasn’t practicing all afternoon for tonight’s gig. But I’m ready to play. And that’s the way I like it. I like to have that little bit of edge. It also depends on who you’re working for. You have to figure the capabilities and limitations of the people that you’re going to play with, and what kind of material you might have to play. Sometimes I’m sure maybe you’ve been on gigs where the piano player brings a fake book, doesn’t know half the tunes, and all of a sudden ninety percent of the repertoire that you’d like to do is by the board so you’ve got to go in another direction. So I think you have to be prepared for that. I just like to play. And I’m the kind of guy, you wake me up at 3:30 in the morning, hand me the horn and say “here’s a half a cup of coffee, let’s blow,” and I’d say okay. Whereas somebody else might tell you to get lost. I just really enjoy playing, and I think that’s what really keeps me going.
Well you’ve got the Montalbano family on tonight and you should be able to play pretty much what you want. © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-

Yeah I really enjoy playing with both of them, they’re both very talented and young Ricky I think is going to really, if he keeps his head on straight, he’s going to make a mark. He already has as far as I’m concerned, or I wouldn’t be using him.
